born.why: The code improves by using trait-based inference (color/smell proxy) to assess safety of new fruits based on past experiences with similar-looking fruits, and prioritizes 'carry' for proven safe foods to build pantry reserves while maintaining strict avoidance of confirmed poisonous items.

The code prioritizes avoiding known poisons and eating proven safe fruits, while using trait-based analogy to infer safety for new species, reducing unnecessary tasting when analogs suggest danger, and increasing willingness to taste unknowns only when hunger is high enough to justify the risk.

The updated code prioritizes carrying known-safe fruits to conserve time, treats any history of harm as a strong deterrent unless the ant is starving (desperation heuristic), and ensures novel fruits are tasted to expand knowledge base only when hunger permits.

The code prioritizes safety by rejecting fruits with harmful trait-history (color-shape combinations), preventing repeated poisoning from similar-looking species, and uses a 'taste' strategy for novel items only when hunger is low enough to afford the risk.

The code prioritizes safety by avoiding fruits with any recorded harm, switches to 'eat' for proven safe items, and uses 'taste' only for unknowns when hunger is sufficiently high to justify the learning cost, ensuring long-term survival through efficient risk management.

The code prioritizes survival by eating unknown fruits only when critically starving, otherwise tasting them to build a safe list, and avoids redundant foraging on known-safe foods unless hunger is high.

The code prioritizes safety by strictly avoiding any fruit species with a history of harm (`harmed=true`), regardless of other traits, because the environment's toxicity can change and past harms are reliable indicators of current danger. It learns from safe experiences (`f>=1`) by carrying or eating them, and only risks tasting unknown fruits when hunger is significant enough to justify the risk but not yet critical, preventing starvation while allowing for discovery.
